evidence: The overall ownership remains coherent: places decides selection, preparation produces flow, the page source owns layout lifetime, the pager owns decoded note resources, and the screen owns the sheet lifetime.
Whole-element notes and empty-anchor notes use the same selection model.
The first-page limit removes the single-page assumption through normal ownership rather than exception masking.

However, clipped raised text has two competing descriptions of its content: retained runs for drawing and inferred original-DOM extent for copying and semantics. The new selection model does not carry enough information across that existing interface.

findings.title: Clipped raised text retains an unbounded original-DOM description for Copy and screen readers
findings.trigger:
Reference n and next as notes, with target markup

Before.Own.Other.

. Open n.
findings.expected: The preview, Copy and screen-reader output contain only Own., with locations belonging to that retained text.
findings.actual: Preparation clips the raised text's inner runs but preserves its original run.node, which names Before. Layout maps the whole raised placeholder to that node. bookUnits then reconstructs raised text from the original document through its parent's end, yielding Before.Own.Other. even though drawing uses the clipped inner runs.

locations.evidence: strip rebuilds RaisedRun with run.node unchanged.
The raised run's node is its original first text node.
Drawing uses the clipped inner text, while the placeholder map retains only node.
Raised text is reconstructed from the original DOM, without the selection boundary.
Copy consumes the same bookUnits output.

sections: 4: One model for the old and the new
designSource.concreteCost: A clipping or omission change must understand an undocumented dependency between preparation, placeholder mapping and DOM-based reconstruction. Drawing and accessibility can disagree because the interface loses the retained content boundaries.

findings.proposedRemedy: Carry the retained original-node content mapping through raised placeholders so drawing, copying and semantics consume the same selection, including omitted holes. Preserve the original DOM. Add the fixture above and assert both semantics and copied text.

findings.title: A large table row still shapes its entire omitted remainder before the preview can stop
findings.trigger: A marked note starts with a table whose first row contains hundreds of ordinary paragraphs in one cell and spans many 12000-pixel pages.
findings.expected: The preview stops shaping after enough divisible content is available for its capacity, retaining the existing exception for an indivisible tall line or image.
findings.actual: PageSource stops only once run.pages becomes nonempty. The table-row path fully lays out every cell before constructing row fragments and publishing pages. Consequently the omitted paragraphs are all shaped and temporarily retained before the first preview page becomes available. Disposing surplus pages afterward does not bound that work or its peak native paragraph storage.

locations.evidence: The stopping condition is first-page availability.
Each cell is fully laid out before the row is emitted.
All row fragments are constructed from the completed cell content.
The bounded-shaping regression exercises ordinary paragraph flow only.

findings.scopeClarification: This is an unmet bound when composing the new preview limit with existing table layout, not a claim that this change introduced the underlying table algorithm. A divisible row is different from the documented indivisible-line/image exception. No phone-performance estimate is asserted.
findings.proposedRemedy: Make the preview capacity effective within table-row work under the existing layout owner. Preserve ordinary table measurements and full-document behavior. Add a tall-row regression that measures shaped units and proves the omitted tail is not fully shaped, alongside cancellation and ownership checks.

findings.title: Backlink omission does not remove block images
findings.trigger: A marked note contains , with img styled display:block, followed by more note text.
findings.expected: The backlink image is omitted and the later note text remains. A note containing only that backlink has no readable preview.
findings.actual: The pager supplies the backlink element in omit, but the ImageItem branch tests only selection membership. The selected block image survives even though its node lies inside an omitted backlink. It can be decoded, drawn and exposed through image semantics.

locations.evidence: Marked backlinks are supplied as omitted elements.
Inline runs apply omitted ranges; ImageItem applies only inside(item.node).

findings.scopeClarification: This omission hole also existed in the earlier excerpt implementation. The changed filtering path still fails the explicit backlink-omission requirement and does not record the gap as deferred work.
findings.proposedRemedy: Apply the same selected-and-not-omitted node rule to block images as to inline content, including images inside table cells. Add regressions for a backlink image followed by retained text and for a backlink-image-only note.
